meta.title: BCO Content Skills Tracker
meta.description: A curated skills tracker for the content design community.

entries.title: Content Engineer
entries.coreFrame: Language infrastructure, AI agents, UX writing, brand communication
entries.quote: This isn’t a traditional content role. We’re looking for someone who operates at the edge of tech and language – someone who can design systems, build agents, and orchestrate tooling that scales quality.

entries.title: Content Systems Architect
entries.coreFrame: AI-powered content production workflows for editorial series
entries.quote: As Content Systems Architect, your job is to own the execution and growth of those series — not by writing content yourself, but by building AI-powered systems.

entries.title: Senior Global UX Writer, Content Systems
entries.coreFrame: Taxonomy, terminology governance, localization architecture, content-as-code
entries.quote: You design content as a scalable system, not isolated screens — shaping taxonomy, terminology, and information architecture to create intuitive and future-proof products.

entries.title: Content Architect
entries.coreFrame: Content modeling, structured data, migrations, governance
entries.quote: By architecting content for both human users and machine learning systems, this role ensures clients capture opportunities across traditional search, generative engine optimization (GEO), and AI-powered experiences.

entries.title: Senior Content Designer, Language Systems
entries.coreFrame: Language governance, AI tool evaluation, design system integration
entries.quote: Build and evolve governance models — including workflows, decision frameworks, review practices, and change‑management processes — that scale content quality across teams.

entries.title: Editor, AI Content Systems
entries.coreFrame: AI editorial QA, prompt workflows, SEO content production
entries.quote: Take the lead on designing, testing, and refining AI workflows and model configurations that produce engaging, accurate editorial content tailored to our brand's unique voice.

entries.title: Annotation Manager — Content Platform
entries.coreFrame: ML data labeling, annotation guidelines, content classification workflows
entries.quote: Translate requirements into clear annotation guidelines, collaborating with content policy experts and updating guidance based on results.

entries.title: Content Designer
entries.coreFrame: Product language infrastructure, terminology systems, AI-generated copy standards, content frameworks
entries.quote: Contribute to product language infrastructure, including glossaries, pattern libraries, review pathways, evaluation rubrics, prompt libraries, and quality guidance.

entries.title: Senior UX Content Designer, Search
entries.coreFrame: AI model behavior design, conversational response strategy, generative AI search UX
entries.quote: In this role, you will drive model behavior design efforts to shape the future of Google's generative AI experiences.

entries.title: Content Design, Vice President
entries.coreFrame: Modular content systems for multi-partner co-brand card portfolio, content architecture, governance, legal/compliance content standards
entries.quote: You will architect and deliver modular, scalable content systems for the Co-Brand portfolio — creating reusable frameworks, templates, and governance that scale across multiple partners and cards while tailoring variants to each partner’s brand, legal requirements, and customer needs.

entries.title: Staff Content Designer, NCXD
entries.coreFrame: Language frameworks, terminology systems, multi-platform content design (TV, mobile, web), globalization partnership, 0-to-1 product initiatives
entries.quote: Known for developing language frameworks and strategies for discovery and engagement across multiple UI platforms, such as TV, mobile and web.

entries.title: Product Content Engineer
entries.coreFrame: GenAI content quality standards, editorial guidelines as reusable frameworks, annotation quality control for model training, measurement frameworks
entries.quote: Strong editorial judgment and creative problem-solving skills, ability to document judgement logic into reusable frameworks to scale across teams.

entries.title: Senior UX Writer and Content Designer, Chrome
entries.coreFrame: Content design for AI Mode features in Chrome, prompt design, system instructions, writing guidelines and word lists, trust and safety content
entries.quote: Consider the user experience, including AI-specific elements like prompt design and system instructions.

entries.title: UX Writer, AI
entries.location: New York or San Francisco (remote in US)
entries.coreFrame: UX writing for AI-powered product features; defining best practices for prompting and interaction patterns; building taxonomies, glossaries, and artifacts for human and agentic ingestion; measuring and evaluating AI-generated language quality

compRange.scope: San Francisco or New York hubs

entries.quote: While the title of this role is “UX Writer,” you might think of yourself as a content engineer as much as a writer — someone who uses language to shape how people interact with AI, from crafting better inputs to defining clear, consistent outputs.

entries.title: Content Strategist | Agentic Commerce
entries.coreFrame: Content architecture for AI-native commerce ecosystems; taxonomy, ontology, and metadata schema design for agent comprehension and retrieval; GEO/AEO content strategy; modular messaging systems for agent-mediated journeys; content governance with experimentation and performance measurement frameworks

entries.title: CX Knowledge Architect
entries.coreFrame: End-to-end CX knowledge system ownership, information architecture, governance, modular reusable content, AI-assisted content QA, taxonomy and tagging
entries.quote: You’ll use Notion as customer zero, building a living system of record structured for both humans and AI — so the right people (and the right agents) can retrieve the right information at the right time.

entries.title: Senior Conversation Designer — Experience Content Design
entries.coreFrame: Conversational experience design, prompt engineering, model behavior guardrails, evaluation frameworks, LLM prototyping, shared patterns and documentation
entries.quote: This role sits at the intersection of writing and system design. You'll bring sharp editorial instincts and real writing chops, but you'll spend your time designing how conversations work — not producing UI copy.

entries.title: AI-Powered Content Systems Specialist
entries.coreFrame: Content strategy as system design, AI-powered content workflows via Jasper, modular templates, AI content standards and guardrails, GEO, marketing enablement
entries.quote: Establish standards for AI-generated content including prompts, templates, tone, guardrails, and quality thresholds.

entries.title: Staff Content Designer, Investing
entries.coreFrame: AI-first content design for complex financial products, content systems and standards, team enablement
entries.quote: Work AI-first. From shipping your own code changes to prototyping and research — you’ll use AI to increase your impact in every part of the product lifecycle.
entries.note: JD explicitly expects content designers to ship their own code changes via AI — a pattern not yet seen elsewhere in the dataset. Potential future signal: autonomous code shipping as part of the content design workflow.

entries.title: UX Writer
entries.coreFrame: UX microcopy, voice and tone frameworks, content patterns, AI-assisted output guardrails in healthcare context
entries.quote: You understand that UX writing is not copywriting with less space. You think in systems, you know why consistency matters, and you're comfortable pushing back when a design choice undercuts the experience.

entries.title: Staff Content Architect
entries.location: New York, Sunnyvale, San Francisco, Mountain View, or Chicago
entries.coreFrame: DITA content model ownership, governance frameworks, metadata and taxonomy alignment, content architecture for AI pipelines and knowledge management systems
entries.quote: Establish and enforce governance frameworks, review mechanisms, and escalation paths to prevent structural drift, duplication, and deviation from defined standards across internal and external contributors.
entries.note: JD frames the role as reducing 'long-term risk and reliance on external consultants' via internal governance frameworks, and sits in a Knowledge Management Solutions team under 'Department: GBO' rather than a product/design org — a placement pattern not yet seen elsewhere in the dataset.

entries.title: UX Writer, Systems
entries.coreFrame: Writing systems governance, design system integration, writing standards codification, AI-leveraged UX writing, guidelines for generated content
entries.quote: Experience using large language models, and an ability to see how they can be leveraged in writing systems.
entries.note: JD explicitly ties accessibility work to UX writing ('Partnering with design on accessibility initiatives'; 'writing optimized for accessibility'). First instance of the accessibility-as-constraint pattern (after the rejected WhatsApp JD); signal created once the Netflix Staff Systems Designer, Language entry showed it a second time.

entries.title: Staff Systems Designer, Language
entries.coreFrame: Language standards encoded into the design system, taxonomy and terminology schemas, AI agent-facing content rules, localization and accessibility as structural constraints
entries.quote: We’re moving beyond buttons and static strings to build the underlying scaffolding that lets AI agents and product experiences communicate safely, naturally, and distinctively across every Netflix surface, in every language, for every audience.

entries.title: AI Information Architect / Content Strategist
entries.coreFrame: Information architecture for self-service support, AI content generation strategy, taxonomy and metadata schemas, IA governance documentation
entries.quote: Leading AI content design and generation strategy, leveraging AI models to produce comprehensive, accurate, and scalable support content at speed.

entries.title: Senior Content Strategist
entries.coreFrame: Editorial governance for help and support content, content quality metrics, automated governance mechanisms, AI solutions for editorial efficiency
entries.quote: Partner with our Insights and Data teams to review and build additional dashboards and tooling to establish more automated governance mechanisms.
entries.note: AI is referenced as part of the work but not specified — the JD says 'AI solutions' twice without naming tools, workflows, or outputs. Comparable support-content entries (Notion, LinkedIn) state theirs concretely. Included on that basis, at the low end of the signal test.

entries.title: Content Architect
entries.coreFrame: Content architecture for AI-first discovery, content models and taxonomies, structured data standards, GEO, cross-functional standards alignment
entries.quote: Define and govern content models, taxonomies, metadata and structured data standards that enable modular, machine-readable, high-performing content.
entries.note: Career area is stated as Marketing, and the role partners with PR and SEO/GEO teams. Included because the stated systems responsibilities — content models, taxonomies, metadata, schema, entity optimization, API integrations — are specific rather than framing. The JD states the placement directly: the role 'sits above channels and formats'.

entries.title: Staff AI Content Designer
entries.coreFrame: Adaptive content for AI-powered surfaces, AI-native design workflow, conversation and interaction patterns, content systems and voice standards across a multi-brand portfolio
entries.quote: Active usage of AI as a core part of your daily workflow includes synthesizing user insights, accelerating discovery, building rapid interactive prototypes (using tools like Claude Code, Gemini, or Figma AI), and closing the gap between design and implementation.
entries.note: The posting files this role under 'Category: Software Engineering' rather than a design, product or marketing function — a placement not seen elsewhere in the dataset. model-behavior-design is assigned on the stated responsibility to shape 'response patterns, interaction flows, and the rhythm of exchanges' for systems customers converse with; the JD also states 'This isn't a chatbot role', and that ambiguity is recorded rather than resolved.

entries.title: Staff Content Strategist, Content Systems Architect
entries.coreFrame: Architecture that implements language standards as working systems, agents and skills that apply standards across domains, AI platform integration, standards-to-system traceability
entries.quote: As Content Systems Architect, you’re responsible for the architecture that turns Adobe’s editorial and AI-generated language standards into working systems.
entries.note: The posting carries a 'What this role Is not' section that explicitly disclaims editorial standard-setting, AI behavior governance, adoption programs, and product-level copy. Those disclaimers are why terminology-governance, ai-content-governance and governance-as-value-prop are not assigned despite surface language that would otherwise support them. The posting also states a separate California range of $189,400-$274,300; the recorded range is the US one, the role being Florida-remote.

entries.title: AI Content Strategy Lead
entries.coreFrame: Knowledge architecture structuring marketing expertise for real-time retrieval by AI agents, content strategy requirements informing AI marketing platform capabilities, governance guardrails and evaluation frameworks for AI-generated content, measurement of AI content system impact
entries.quote: Design the knowledge architecture that structures customer insights, brand voice, audience context, messaging frameworks, and campaign intelligence for real-time access by AI agents and content generation systems.

entries.title: Taxonomist, Content Design
entries.coreFrame: Taxonomy, ontology, and controlled-vocabulary design across product surfaces; governance standards, naming conventions, and metadata schemas for consistency at scale; cross-functional integration with search, recommendation, and localization systems; data- and research-driven validation of classification systems
entries.quote: Design, build, and maintain taxonomies, ontologies, and controlled vocabularies that support content organization and navigation across Meta products and platforms.

entries.title: Senior Manager Content Designer (Individual Contributor)
entries.location: McLean, VA | Richmond, VA | New York, NY
entries.coreFrame: Foundational content systems, voice guidelines, and structured prompt libraries that let product design teams write independently; taxonomy and logic ownership for high-leverage content initiatives; narrative quality auditing across live product experiences; mentoring and enablement to mature the content design practice within a cross-functional pod
entries.quote: Instead of focusing only on isolated product screens, you will focus on building the foundational tools — including content design systems, voice guidelines, and structured prompt libraries — that empower broader product design teams to handle day-to-day writing tasks independently.

entries.title: Sr. UX Conversation Designer, Amazon Customer Service
entries.coreFrame: Conversation design and voice/tone/personality for customer service chatbots and web/app experiences, A/B testing and research on voice, tone, and messaging, involvement in building AI and LLMs, writing guidelines for conversation and content design
entries.quote: You'll also be involved in building AI and Large Language Models (LLMs), creating writing guidelines to raise the bar, and share our expertise with our product and tech partners.

entries.title: Senior Staff UX Writer, International
entries.coreFrame: Standing up the UX Writing function within a newly forming Global Markets team — workflows, partnerships, and standards; localized product language for country-specific features across Italy, Germany, Spain, France and the UK; cross-functional collaboration with country managers, localization experts, linguists, and translators; mentoring and reviewing other UX writers; alignment with the central UX Writing team on shared voice and quality standards
entries.quote: Define and drive the UX Writing function within Global Markets, establishing workflows, partnerships, and standards for a newly forming team, including reviewing and mentoring other UX writers.

entries.title: Principal AI Model Designer
entries.coreFrame: Designing the Wise Assistant conversational AI system for Support — architecting agents, owning prompts, and defining how context and knowledge are used to resolve customer problems; shaping agent behaviour and how system components interact; raising design maturity and context engineering understanding within the Support squad; role sits within the Content Design Guild alongside Content Designers
entries.quote: You're an accomplished and experienced Model Designer, or a systems-focused Content Designer who has already made this transition in your day-to-day work.
entries.note: The JD places the role within the "Content Design Guild" as part of the Design team, stating the disciplines "share a common skill set and design process," and frames Model Designer and systems-focused Content Designer as two entry paths into the same role. This is the clearest instance in the corpus of the dataset's "model design" vocabulary term appearing as an actual job title while the role still organizationally reports through a content design function.

entries.title: Staff AI Content Designer, FinCrime
entries.coreFrame: Content design strategy across FinCrime's cross-functional teams, balancing regulatory obligations with customer experience; using AI to scale content design impact and as part of the content design toolkit; standardising and systematising experiences with design leaders from other squads; owning the squad's content end-to-end and raising content design quality and maturity within FinCrime; part of the Content Guild, collaborating with the content community across Wise
entries.quote: You'll be figuring out how to harness the potential of AI to scale your impact as a content designer, quickly test and iterate on your ideas with a huge degree of freedom and flexibility, and learn as part of your day-to-day work as this technology evolves.

entries.title: Senior Content Strategist (Core UX)
entries.coreFrame: UX writing and content strategy across Coupang's app and services — defining writing principles, terminology, and content frameworks and propagating them org-wide; proposing content strategy from the customer journey and UX principles in collaboration with PMs and designers. Extends into AI-generated content experience design — establishing behavioral guidelines, response formats, and quality rubrics for AI-generated content, defining Korean voice & tone for conversational AI, and collaborating with engineers to write pass/fail quality rules and redefine format and tone guidelines as requirements for model training and prompt improvement.
entries.quote: Redefines format and tone guidelines into requirements that engineers can use for model training and prompt improvement.

entries.title: Content Engineer
entries.coreFrame: B2B technology content development across long-form and campaign assets for enterprise clients; developing prompts, prompt patterns, reusable instructions, and workflow templates for AI-assisted drafting, editing, and content repurposing; pressure-testing AI-generated outputs for hallucinations, generic language, and unsupported claims, and building QA checklists and editorial review standards for AI-supported content workflows; documenting repeatable workflows — source requirements, prompt inputs, review steps, QA criteria — as part of an evolving Human + AI content operating model; helping train and enable teammates on AI-supported workflows.
entries.quote: Develop prompts, prompt patterns, reusable instructions, and workflow templates that improve content quality and production speed.

entries.title: Staff AI Conversation Designer
entries.coreFrame: Conversation and model design for an agentic AI Assistant used across Gen's brands — dialogue flows, prompt structures, model persona and tone, error and fallback handling, and multi-turn interaction patterns; reviewing model outputs and agent behavior for quality, safety, and consistency; building reusable conversation frameworks, prompt libraries, and evaluation criteria; and acting as design lead for the AI Assistant platform team, partnering with each brand's product and design teams to integrate the assistant's behavior with brand-owned UI.
entries.quote: You will shape how our AI Assistant thinks, speaks, and acts, defining the conversation flows, prompt structures, and behavioral standards that make agentic AI experiences feel trustworthy, capable, and human-centered.

entries.title: Content Designer, Language & Systems
entries.coreFrame: Tooling, documentation, standards, and evaluation workflows within the Writers Guild that make it possible to generate and update UX content at scale, reliably and consistently, in line with Wix's guidelines; defining content governance across both human and agentic workflows; building programmatic style guides, evaluation frameworks, reusable UI patterns, and rule-based terminology systems intended as the authoritative source of truth org-wide; mentoring UX writers and educating writers and non-writers on these systems and best practices; championing AI tool adoption through workshops and guild content reviews; and collaborating with product localization on frameworks that scale across languages, regions, and assistive technology contexts.
entries.quote: You'll be central to defining how content governance works across both human and agentic workflows, while also educating writers and non-writers on these systems and best practices.

entries.title: AI Content Strategist
entries.coreFrame: Building an AI-driven automated content production system within the Global Content Strategy & Design team — covering requirements analysis, prompt design, content generation, channel adaptation, quality evaluation, and asset accumulation across online promotions, campaign pages, ad creative, and multilingual marketing content; establishing AI content standards and quality evaluation mechanisms; building industry terminology, prompt libraries, and content templates as reusable knowledge assets; and judging which content suits AI mass-production versus human refinement.
entries.quote: This role isn't just about using AI to generate content — it requires understanding business goals, product UX/UI, brand voice, channel strategy, and B2B industry differences, to judge what content is suited to AI mass-production versus what needs human refinement, and how to safeguard content quality through standards, templates, terminology banks, industry insight, and evaluation mechanisms.

entries.title: Content Design Lead - Evinova
entries.coreFrame: Setting the direction and quality bar for content design and content strategy across the team while staying hands-on with content design on the most critical experiences; owning and maintaining Evinova's Content Design Guidance document, keeping tone of voice, terminology, and content patterns current as products and the regulatory landscape evolve; partnering with the Product team to shape end-to-end experiences, with the Translation and Localization team to extend the Guidance across languages and markets, and with the Content Delivery team to get content into the product; running cross-functional working sessions to upskill product, design, and localization peers on content standards; championing AI-first ways of working by identifying opportunities to use AI to expedite the content design process — from drafting and editing to consistency checks and content operations — while retaining a human-in-the-loop approach; and mentoring content designers while establishing a systematic approach for integrating content design patterns into the Evinova Design System.
entries.quote: Champion AI-first ways of working, including identifying and embedding opportunities to use AI to expedite the content design process while simultaneously raising quality, from drafting and editing to consistency checks and content operations, while ensuring that AI processes retain a human-in-the-loop approach.

entries.title: Technical Documentation and Content Engineer, Claude Docs
entries.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
entries.coreFrame: Owning documentation for Claude apps across multiple product surfaces (Claude.ai, Cowork, Claude Tag, Claude Science) written by many teams — the unification layer of information architecture, editorial standards, and style guide for the Claude Docs site; designing, building, and running automated documentation systems, including self-healing pipelines, AI-assisted review and maintenance, and quality guardrails; establishing the conventions and tooling product teams use to keep their own documentation accurate and consistent; curating contributions from across the company for clarity and consistency; and defining and tracking measures of content quality and discoverability.
entries.quote: This is a content + systems ownership role. You'll curate and set the bar for what others write, and you'll build the automation that enforces it: self-healing pipelines, AI-assisted review and maintenance, and the conventions each product team follows to keep their own docs healthy.

entries.title: Staff Content Designer
entries.coreFrame: Serving as Bolt's first content designer, with the role split between setting the content standard (voice, terminology, and patterns for recurring product moments such as prompts, errors, empty states, permissions, billing, and settings) and, after the initial period, shipping content-led features end to end as sole design DRI — scoping, designing in Figma or building with agentic tools, and driving through implementation without a product design partner. Also reviewing others' writing to raise its quality, owning content strategy input into product direction, and partnering with Marketing and CX across the user lifecycle.
entries.quote: You can take a content-led feature from problem to shipped without a product designer. That means designing it in Figma, or building it with agentic tools, to a standard we'd actually ship.

entries.title: Lead Conversational Designer - Agentic Experiences
entries.location: Lowell, MA; Seattle, WA; or Sunrise, FL
entries.coreFrame: Building and evolving the behavioral systems that shape how UKG's Bryte AI agents respond and act — conversation response patterns, ontologies and structured content models, and prompt and interaction frameworks. Defining how agents operate across a spectrum of autonomy from suggesting to confirming to acting on the user's behalf, and designing for trust, compliance, and human-in-the-loop decision making within HCM contexts. Iterating on interaction strategies and system behaviors through experimentation, and building patterns that make AI behavior explainable, predictable, and controllable.
entries.quote: Develop and extend ontologies and structured content systems that enable scalable, consistent AI behavior.

entries.title: Principal Conversational AI Designer
entries.coreFrame: Leading the design of conversational experiences across UnitedHealth Group's AI-powered products and services, applying conversation design and Agentic AI expertise to create AI interactions and defining best practices for prompt engineering, styling, and design documentation across personas. Using AI tools throughout the product design lifecycle and defining design tool features to support prompt design iteration and testing. Designing personalized interactions that adapt to individual users over time. Coaching and mentoring conversation designers and cross-functional partners, and partnering with product, engineering, and operations teams to define and test analytics approaches measuring conversation effectiveness and business impact.
entries.quote: As a Principal Conversational AI Designer, you will lead the design of conversational experiences that help consumers accomplish their goals through UnitedHealth Group's AI-powered products and services.
entries.note: The posting's page header titles the role "Principal UX CX Designer" (requisition 2382279), but the body text self-describes it as "Principal Conversational AI Designer" from the first sentence onward and consistently thereafter. The `title` field stores the body's self-description, which is also the string the quote and cluster/signal assignments are drawn from.

entries.title: Senior Interaction Designer (Conversation)
entries.coreFrame: Designing conversational and multimodal AI experiences for GOV.UK, including GOV.UK Chat and agentic experiences, and prototyping and testing dialogue patterns, prompts, and interaction flows with real users. Exploring multiple approaches to solving user problems through conversation and natural language, and feeding into the development of AI conversation design principles and reusable dialogue patterns for government. Collaborating with product, research, engineering, and other designers to deliver joined-up services, and helping establish conversation design as a discipline at GDS through a community of practice and by sharing knowledge and skills across teams.
entries.quote: help establish conversation design as a discipline at GDS, contributing to a community of practice, sharing knowledge across teams, and helping others develop their skills in this emerging area
entries.note: First UK government entry in the dataset, and the first entry outside a corporate employer. Also the first GBP-denominated compRange. The posting states three overlapping compensation figures: a headline range (£56,850-£71,920), a per-location base point figure, and a capability-based range per location (£62,120-£71,920 London / £57,350-£67,150 National Locations, i.e. Bristol and Manchester). The recorded range is the capability-based London figure, following the largest-co-equal-city rule. `covers` is left null rather than resolved to `base`: a separate sentence labels a different, single-point figure as base salary, but this range is described as scaling with a specialist pay allowance on top of that base, which does not cleanly match either the `base` or `total` definition.

entries.title: Staff Content Designer
entries.coreFrame: Writing and shaping content across the purchase journey — landing pages, onboarding, checkout, post-purchase, and microcopy — and building the narrative backbone for major product flows. Contributing to Ethos's content standards, tone-of-voice guidelines, and review processes alongside design leadership. Using AI tools and frameworks to produce on-brand content faster, and helping shape AI tools that let others generate content with the correct tone, structure, and guardrails. Grounding the work in customer research, competitive audits, analytics, and A/B testing.
entries.quote: Help to shape AI tools that can empower others to generate content with the correct tone, structure, and necessary guardrails.

entries.title: Senior Content Strategist, Product Enablement
entries.coreFrame: Owns narrative architecture and technical enablement across the product ecosystem: strategy and authoring for the developer hub, API specs, and integration guides, partnering with Marketing to co-build messaging platforms and terminology standards, connecting Engineering, Product Design, Customer Success, and Marketing around product rollouts, and using AI tools to offload routine writing so effort concentrates on technical narratives and enablement assets. Reports to the VP, Experience Design.
entries.quote: Partner directly with Marketing to co-build core messaging platforms, terminology standards, and voice-and-tone frameworks, ensuring unified positioning across product enablement, demand generation campaigns, and sales collateral.

entries.title: Senior Content Designer
entries.coreFrame: Owning product and member-facing copy across in-app flows, onboarding, notifications, action plans, empty states, and error handling. Defining and stewarding the brand voice across surfaces and contributors, and reviewing copy org-wide beyond the role's own output. Working upstream of design decisions alongside Product Design and PMM, and using AI tooling (named: Claude, Cursor) to accelerate ideation, drafting, and iteration.
entries.quote: You use AI tooling actively. Claude, Cursor, or equivalent — to accelerate ideation, draft generation, and iteration without sacrificing voice quality.

entries.title: Content Design Lead
entries.coreFrame: Setting the quality bar for content design across a team of six embedded Content Designers, and building craft infrastructure — frameworks, guidelines, tooling, and content systems — that scales across those embedded teams. Deepening how content design is embedded in the product development lifecycle across Product, Design, Engineering, and Research; enabling Content Designer growth through direct leadership, mentorship, or community-building depending on team structure; defining metrics that demonstrate content design's value to the broader organisation; and driving operational efficiency across the function. The posting states the org structure is still evolving, and this may involve direct people leadership, a guild model built on craft authority, or both.
entries.quote: You'll shape the direction of the function through standards, tooling, and craft infrastructure that enables a distributed team to do their best work.
entries.note: The posting's job-board header titles the role "Content Design Manager," but the body text self-describes it as "Content Design Lead" from the opening sentence of the role overview onward, and consistently thereafter — the header title appears once and is never reinforced. The `title` field stores the body's self-description. Separately, the JD states a gross monthly salary range ("€4.917—€6.650 EUR"), the first monthly-stated figure in the corpus; every other entry states an annual figure. `compRange` is recorded as null rather than displayed: the schema has no period field, annualizing would assume a bonus or 13th-month structure the JD never states, and recording the bare monthly numbers would misrepresent them as an annual figure to a reader comparing across entries.

entries.title: Senior Content Designer
entries.coreFrame: End-to-end content strategy and execution across the product, from framing concepts to microcopy, as the company's first Content Designer. Establishing the conventions, systems, libraries, style guides, tools, and AI skills the company relies on for language consistency as it scales, and consulting on content management and translation tooling for multi-language product experience. Also named: user research and experimentation to define user needs and behaviors, jumping into incidents to support crisis messaging and recovery comms, and occasional graphic design and copywriting for marketing materials (investor decks, pitch decks, the company website) as part of the small Design team's shared brand-building work.
entries.quote: Establish the conventions, systems, libraries, style guides, tools and AI skills that Relay relies on to ensure consistency of language as we scale and diversify our product experiences.

entries.title: Experience Design Lead
entries.location: New York, NY; Atlanta, GA; Seattle, WA; or Indianapolis, IN
entries.coreFrame: Setting the design and content quality bar for a team building AI and automation tools for internal Customer Success Managers — contributing UX writing, information architecture, and content direction on product features from early sprint stages through delivery; owning voice, tone, and content standards across Skills copy, product documentation, and field-facing materials; and building lightweight design and content guidelines the team can use. Also named: producing polished decks and communications for field, ops, and leadership audiences, and auditing existing assets against how they're documented or delivered. The posting frames the role as craft rather than strategy.
entries.quote: The ideal background here is UX writing or content design — someone who's sat on a product team, worked in sprint cycles, and knows how to translate complex product thinking into clear, useful language.
entries.note: The posting's job-board metadata files this role under "Job Category: Program & Project Management," a category that matches neither the title nor the described work, which is content-design craft on UX writing, IA, and content standards. `content-adjacent` is assigned because the title ("Experience Design Lead") and that job-board category sit outside titles the field recognizes as content design or UX writing, while the body states directly that "the ideal background here is UX writing or content design" and the stated responsibilities are content-design craft work — the same pattern as the Spotify Annotation Manager, Meta Product Content Engineer, and Notion CX Knowledge Architect entries. The JD's only AI-tooling line ("Experience making AI tools or technical products accessible... for non-technical audiences is a major plus") sits in the preferred-qualifications section, not a stated responsibility, so ai-native-expectation and ai-tooling are not assigned; enabler-not-bottleneck is not assigned either, since the posting states directly "This isn't a strategy role — it's a craft role. You'll get your hands dirty, ship things fast." The role's scope — owning quality for internally-consumed artifacts (decks, Slack messages, prototypes, field-facing materials) rather than product-surface content — is a single instance in the corpus so far and is not reflected in any cluster or signal assignment.

terminology-governance.label: Terminology & language governance
terminology-governance.description: Companies are asking content designers to own the language layer, building glossaries, controlled vocabularies, and a single source of truth for product language. The pattern holds across industries, not one sector.

content-systems-design.label: Content systems design
content-systems-design.description: The most common cluster in the dataset. Companies want someone who designs content as a system: frameworks, patterns, reusable templates that scale past a single screen.

ai-tooling.label: AI tooling & automation
ai-tooling.description: Building and operationalizing AI-powered workflows is now a stated expectation in most roles we're tracking. This goes beyond using AI tools. Companies want someone who can evaluate, configure, and own the workflow end to end.

ai-content-governance.label: AI-generated content governance
ai-content-governance.description: As AI-generated content scales, someone has to own the quality standards. Rubrics, prompt guidelines, tone constraints, guardrails. This responsibility is growing fast in the dataset.

taxonomy.label: Taxonomy & information architecture
taxonomy.description: Classification and information architecture are showing up in content design roles that didn't ask for them a few years ago. Content designers who can build and maintain structured content models are increasingly valuable, especially where AI needs clean inputs.

localization.label: Localization & internationalization
localization.description: Writing for localization is a consistent ask in global product roles. Structuring strings, managing variables, keeping source copy translation-ready. Not new, but a clear differentiator when you can demonstrate it.

enablement.label: Enablement & team upskilling
enablement.description: Content design teams are shrinking, and it's increasingly common to be a one-person centralized resource. The roles we're tracking are hiring for the ability to build playbooks, guidelines, and tools that scale content quality across teams, not to write everything yourself.

technical-writing.label: Technical writing & documentation
technical-writing.description: Documenting complex systems is appearing in content roles that wouldn't have asked for it before. Governance models, data structures, platform logic. A signal that content designers are being pulled closer to the technical layer.

ai-native-expectation.label: AI fluency expected
ai-native-expectation.description: AI fluency is listed as a baseline in most roles we're tracking. If you're not actively working with AI tools, this is the most urgent gap the data shows.

enabler-not-bottleneck.label: Enabler, not bottleneck
enabler-not-bottleneck.description: These roles are hiring someone to build systems that let others write well, not someone to write everything themselves. A consistent signal that the solo-writer model is losing ground.

governance-as-value-prop.label: Governance emphasized
governance-as-value-prop.description: Governance is the primary deliverable in these roles, not a background process. Companies are hiring for the ability to set standards and make them stick across teams.

title-dilution.label: Title outpaces the work
title-dilution.description: A “content systems” title doesn't always mean content systems work. Some postings borrow the language to describe editorial or marketing work instead. Read the responsibilities, not the title.

title-responsibility-gap.label: Work outpaces the title
title-responsibility-gap.description: The title undersells what the role actually requires. If you're screening on title alone, you may be missing roles where the scope and seniority exceed what the name suggests.

model-behavior-design.label: Model behavior design
model-behavior-design.description: A growing number of roles are asking content designers to shape how AI models actually respond, not just write around them. An emerging space where content design and machine learning overlap directly.

language-infrastructure.label: Language as infrastructure
language-infrastructure.description: When a job description frames language work as “infrastructure,” it signals the company sees content as a foundational system, not a production task. These roles tend to sit closer to platform and engineering teams.

content-adjacent.label: Content work under new titles
content-adjacent.description: Content skills like taxonomy, governance, and documentation are being applied in roles that aren't content design jobs. The demand is there under titles the field doesn't recognize yet.

classification-for-ml.label: Classification for ML
classification-for-ml.description: Taxonomy and classification skills are showing up in roles that feed machine learning systems. Content designers who've built tagging schemas or content models have transferable value in AI-adjacent contexts.

content-marketing-adjacent.label: Content systems for marketers
content-marketing-adjacent.description: Roles that specialize in content architecture, taxonomy governance, and AI output standards are being hired into marketing orgs, not just product and design. The systems responsibilities are substantive. What's different is where they sit.

geo-seo.label: GEO & SEO
geo-seo.description: Content architecture for generative engine optimization is showing up as an explicit responsibility. GEO is newer than SEO. It's about structuring content so AI systems can find and cite it, not just humans.

structured-data.label: Structured data
structured-data.description: A small number of roles are asking content designers to work with Schema.org, JSON-LD, or entity modeling. Early signal, but it points toward content designers owning more of the technical stack.

accessibility-as-constraint.label: Accessibility as structural constraint
accessibility-as-constraint.description: Accessibility is showing up alongside localization as a structural requirement the content architecture has to support, not a late-stage copy pass. A small but recurring pattern worth watching.

central-standards-function.label: Central standards function
central-standards-function.description: Content standards owned by one central or horizontal function, with distributed teams consuming them inside set guardrails. Roles describe sitting above channels, acting as a single accountable owner, or publishing playbooks other teams adapt. It's a structural answer to where content work sits, distinct from embedding writers directly in product teams.

agent-retrieval.label: Structured for agent retrieval
agent-retrieval.description: Content structured so AI systems can retrieve and apply it at generation time. This sits apart from search optimization and schema markup — it's the knowledge layer a model reads from before it writes. A small pattern so far, and it places content work upstream of the output rather than after it.
